title: Non-blocking finding from PR #315's review (backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-signal-engine-followups)
description: Non-blocking finding from pr-reviewer's full review of PR #315 (backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-signal-engine-followups), which accepted the PR -- backend suite (1341 passed, 100% line/branch coverage), ruff/mypy/profit-target-wording-guard/validate_tasks.py all clean, no API surface touched (no OpenAPI regen needed), no UI surface (no browser walkthrough/e2e needed). The `score_volume_confirmation` keep-as-is rationale (rolling-average-scale-mismatch argument) was independently checked and is analytically sound: `analyse_day_trader` maps `intermediate_ohlcv` onto `analyse()`'s `daily_ohlcv` parameter, so both `latest_volume` and its 20-period rolling average are computed from the same (intermediate-leg) series in day-trader mode exactly as in swing mode, and swapping only the numerator to `short_term_ohlcv`'s much-finer-grained latest bar while leaving the denominator computed from the coarser intermediate leg would indeed systematically bias that arm toward reading 'below average' (a finer bar's volume is mechanically smaller than a coarser leg's per-bar rolling average), confirming the PR's reasoning rather than just trusting it.

checklist.step: `docs/Analyse.md` §6's "Volume confirmation ... trigger bar volume is above 20-day average" row is not updated to document the day-trader-mode-specific behavior this PR's `decisions` entry and `app/signals/engine.py` docstring/comment now describe in detail: that the volume-confirmation component deliberately continues comparing the *intermediate* leg's latest bar/rolling average even in day-trader mode, not the actual short-term leg Trigger itself now evaluates against. `docs/Analyse.md` §2's Screen 3 bullet and §9's "partially resolved" note both got a parallel day-trader-mode footnote when Screen 3 itself changed (PR #312) -- §6's table has no equivalent footnote for this narrower, OR'd-with-Force-Index-spike component, so a reader of Analyse.md alone (without cross-referencing `engine.py`'s docstring or this task's `decisions` entry) would not learn that "trigger bar volume" is not literally what day-trader mode computes here. Not blocking (the original checklist item that prompted this PR only asked for a decision to be recorded, which it was, via docstring/inline-comment/`decisions` entry), but worth adding a short parallel footnote to §6 (or a cross-reference to the `decisions` entry) so the methodology doc stays the single source of truth without requiring a reader to already know to look elsewhere.

decisions.decision: Added a day-trader-mode footnote to docs/Analyse.md §6's "Volume confirmation" table row, appended to the existing "Scoring" cell rather than as a separate table or a numbered footnote marker below the table.
decisions.rationale: Matched the existing style §2's Screen 3 bullet (line 77) and §9's Screen 3 note (line 384) already use for this exact kind of day-trader-mode caveat: a bolded '**Day-trader mode** (`task-id`): ...' clause appended directly onto the pre-existing prose it qualifies, in-line, rather than a separate footnote apparatus -- both of those precedents modify the sentence/bullet in place instead of adding an asterisk/superscript marker plus a below-the-table note. A markdown table cell can hold arbitrarily long prose (this doc already has far longer single lines elsewhere, e.g. §2's Force Index bullet), so no table-structure change was needed. Content-wise, the footnote restates (in the reader-facing terms §6 itself uses -- 'intermediate leg' vs 'short-term leg', 'rolling average', 'trigger bar volume') the same keep-as-is rationale already recorded in app/signals/engine.py's `analyse()` docstring paragraph near `short_term_ohlcv` and in `backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-signal-engine-followups`'s own `decisions` entry (the rolling-average-scale-mismatch argument, independently re-verified sound by both that task's pr-reviewer and pr-decision passes), and points back to that task by id for the full derivation rather than duplicating the entire multi-paragraph rationale into the methodology doc itself. This closes the gap PR #315's review flagged: a reader of Analyse.md alone, without cross-referencing engine.py or the task board, can now learn that 'trigger bar volume' is not literally what day-trader mode computes for this component, matching what §2/§9 already do for Screen 3 itself.
